search_hits.title: Urban Gentrification Metrics: Four Decades of American City Transformation (the exemplar report)
search_hits.snippet: The operator's exemplar report (vendored as source-report.pdf): New York City leads with a Gini coefficient of 0.5469 versus the national average of 0.40 in 2013, while Atlanta and Miami follow at 0.57 and New Orleans at 0.56; the Case-Shiller Index reached 325.78 in July 2024 (+225% since January 2000); 48 of the 50 largest metros saw worsening mobility with Houston the sole improvement (+1.1%).

search_hits.title: Cities Where Income Inequality Is Highest and Lowest in 2024
search_hits.snippet: SmartAsset ranked 98 of the largest U.S. cities by income inequality, measured by comparing the incomes of the top 80% of earners with the bottom 20%. New Orleans tops the list with a ratio of 7.87; Boston follows with 7.81 ($172,476 at the 80th percentile versus $22,095 at the 20th).

search_hits.title: Since the pandemic, young adults have fueled the revival of small towns and rural areas
search_hits.snippet: Manufacturing jobs, which peaked at 19.5 million in 1979, fell to under 11.5 million during the pandemic, while employment in finance and professional and business services soared from 12 million to 32 million; nearly 80 percent of the country's growth in its under-45 population has been concentrated in metro areas with over a million residents.
